target_audience: University freshmen and AP Calculus students

sections.title: The Mystery of the Tangled Equation
lecture_lines: Explicit functions isolate y on one side clearly.
Implicit equations leave x and y tangled together.
Solving for y can create multiple complex pieces.
Implicit differentiation handles these equations without rearranging.
It treats the relationship as a single cohesive rule.
animations: Show the equation y = 2x + 3 in #00FF00 (green). Draw a clear box around the 'y'.
Show x^2 + y^2 = 25 in #FF00FF (magenta). Draw a swirling arrow around x^2 and y^2 to show they are 'tangled'.
Transform x^2 + y^2 = 25 into y = ±sqrt(25 - x^2). Flash the ± symbol in #FFFF00 (yellow) to show complexity.
Return to x^2 + y^2 = 25. A 'magic wand' (star shape) glows near the equation in #00FFFF (cyan).
Draw a thick #FFFFFF (white) border surrounding the entire x^2 + y^2 = 25 equation to represent a single rule.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Chain Rule 'Sidekick'
lecture_lines: Treat y as a hidden function of x.
Apply the Chain Rule whenever differentiating y-terms.
Multiply by dy over dx for every y-derivative.
animations: Show 'y' and then transform it into 'y(x)' with a subtle glow in #00FF00 to represent a hidden function.
Show the expression d/dx[y^3]. Draw an arrow pointing from the exponent 3 down to create 3y^2.
Add '· dy/dx' next to 3y^2 in #FF00FF. Highlight 'dy/dx' with a scale-up pulse animation.

sections.title: The Strategy: The 'Level Playing Field'
lecture_lines: Apply the d over dx operator to both sides.
Differentiate every term to keep the equation balanced.
This finds the slope without isolating y first.
animations: Show a generic equation f(x,y) = g(x,y). Place 'd/dx[...]' operators around both sides in #00FFFF.
Display a balance scale icon in #FFFFFF; as the d/dx operators are applied, the scale remains level.
The symbol 'dy/dx' appears in #FFFF00 next to the equation, representing the slope found without isolation.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Walkthrough: The Circular Track
lecture_lines: Differentiate each term: two x plus two y dy dx.
The derivative of the constant twenty-five is zero.
Group terms with dy over dx on one side.
Factor out dy over dx and divide to isolate.
At point (3, 4), the slope is negative three-fourths.
animations: Display x^2 + y^2 = 25. Below it, write '2x + 2y · dy/dx' term by term in #00FF00.
Complete the equation: '2x + 2y · dy/dx = 0'. Highlight the '0' in #FF0000 (red) for emphasis.
Move 2x to the right side to show '2y · dy/dx = -2x'. Use #FF00FF for the new right-hand side.
Show division by 2y to isolate: 'dy/dx = -x/y'. Draw a #00FFFF box around this final formula.
Substitute x=3, y=4 into -x/y. Draw a circle and a tangent line at point (3,4) with slope -3/4.

sections.title: Visualizing the Slope Field
lecture_lines: This method works even when the vertical line test fails.
Calculate slopes anywhere on complex loops or curves.
Watch the tangent line change along the Folium of Descartes.
animations: Show the Folium of Descartes curve. Draw a vertical red line (#FF0000) that intersects the curve at two points.
Multiple points along the complex loop of the curve light up in #00FF00.
A tangent line in #FFFF00 glides along the curve, rotating in real-time to match the calculated slope.

sections.title: Final Summary & Pro-Tips
lecture_lines: Differentiate every term, including constants which become zero.
Always attach the dy over dx tag to y-derivatives.
Solve for dy over dx using basic algebra.
This technique is the foundation for related rates problems.
Mastery of these steps makes complex calculus much easier.
animations: Display a checklist. Check the first box: 'Differentiate all terms (constants = 0)' in #00FF00.
Check the second box: 'Attach dy/dx to y-derivatives'. Pulse the 'dy/dx' text in #FF00FF.
Check the third box: 'Isolate dy/dx using algebra'. Show a generic formula 'dy/dx = ...' boxed in #00FFFF.
The words 'Related Rates' appear in #FF00FF with an arrow pointing from the completed checklist.
The entire checklist glows #00FF00 and the title 'Mastery Achieved' appears in bold.
